hints: Focus on what addition polymerisation actually does to a C=C double bond, it opens it to make two new single bonds.
Notice the double bond is inside a ring, so the ring itself does not open, the two carbons of the old double bond each gain one link to another monomer.
Look for the structure where each six-membered ring joins the chain at two adjacent carbons, the original C=C carbons.
walkthrough:
**Recall addition polymerisation**

Think simply. A C=C double bond breaks open to give two single bonds that link to neighbours.

$$\text{C=C} \rightarrow \text{-C-C-}$$

**Apply this to cyclohexene**

Cyclohexene is a 6-membered ring with one C=C. The ring stays intact, only the pi bond opens.

So each $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$ monomer becomes a $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}$ repeat unit where the two carbons that were double bonded now each form a new C-C bond to another ring.

**Find the 1,2-linkage**

That means in the polymer, every cyclohexane ring must be connected to the chain at two adjacent carbons.

Only the structure with neighbouring rings joined 1,2 to 1,2 shows this pattern, with the continuation bonds on adjacent carbons of each ring.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows rings linked at opposite (1,4) positions with the chain going straight through. The original double bond carbons in cyclohexene are adjacent, not opposite, so this linkage is impossible.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows rings linked with continuation bonds in 1,3 type positions. This is a common trap if you do not check carefully that the two bonds on each ring must be on neighbouring carbons from the opened C=C.
options.C: Correct. The double bond opens and each of the two adjacent carbons bonds to another monomer. This gives a chain of cyclohexane rings joined at adjacent carbons, exactly as shown, with the continuation bonds on neighbouring carbons of each ring.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows a spiro structure where two rings share a single carbon atom. Addition polymerisation forms two separate new bonds per monomer, it never fuses two rings onto one common atom.
